title: NY State Assembly · District 45
area: Brooklyn: Sheepshead Bay, Midwood, Manhattan Beach, Gravesend, and Brighton Beach

context.text: Both major-party primaries for this seat were canceled. Incumbent Michael Novakhov (R, C) advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries without appearing on the ballot. Joey Cohen-Saban (D) advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot; he also has the Fight Anti-Semitism Party line. A third candidate, Rene Mitchell (Independent), withdrew before the general election. Cohen-Saban lost to Novakhov by about 230 votes in the 2024 general election and is running again.

summary.text: Michael Novakhov is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent in Assembly District 45, representing Sheepshead Bay, Midwood, Manhattan Beach, Gravesend, and Brighton Beach. He was first elected in November 2022, unseating Democratic incumbent Steven Cymbrowitz, who had represented the district since 2001, and is seeking a third term.

background.text: Emigrated from the former USSR with his family.
Worked for about 20 years in radio broadcasting; in 2019 he co-founded Freedom FM, which he describes as the most-listened-to Russian-language radio station in the country.

priorities.text: "Michael has proudly served his community as Assemblymember for the 45th District since 2023... [and has] put forward and co-sponsored over 200 pieces of legislation that will significantly improve our quality of life."
Public safety: says he is combatting rising crime, particularly hate crimes targeting the AAPI and Jewish communities, and opposes New York's bail-reform laws.
Affordability: says he wants to make health care and housing more affordable for constituents.

positions.summary: Sponsor of a bill (A5201) to repeal New York City's congestion-pricing law and establish an MTA committee to survey transit-infrastructure and ADA-compliance needs instead.
Says he is committed to expanding school-choice options, including charter schools, private schools, and homeschooling.
positions.quote: I am committed to expanding school choice options, including charter schools, private schools, and homeschooling, to provide families with the flexibility they need to navigate the educational journey of their children.

positions.summary: Platform calls for expanding the reach of the state's Health and Hospital system, expanding Medicaid coverage of long-term residential care, and expanding pharmaceutical insurance coverage.

Says he will continue advocating for policies that strengthen the U.S.-Israel relationship; opposed a state bill ('Not on Our Dime') that would have restricted nonprofit dealings with Israel, and sponsored a bill (A5214) barring nonprofits from supporting groups like Hamas.
positions.quote: I will continue to advocate for policies that strengthen the bond between the United States and Israel, uphold our shared values, and combat anti-Semitism in all its forms.

record.text: Prime sponsor of a bill (A5201) to repeal New York City's congestion pricing law and create an MTA committee to survey infrastructure and ADA-compliance needs; introduced February 2025, referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee.

Sponsor of the 'Not on our dollar!: Ending New York funding of Hamas violence act' (A5214), which would bar not-for-profit corporations from unauthorized support of Hamas and other groups that fund Middle East terrorism, with civil penalties and a private right of action; held in the Ways and Means Committee as of the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsor of a resolution (K.58) commemorating the Holocaust.
Sponsor of legislation (A3694-A) mandating measures at colleges and universities to deter and combat hate crimes on campus.
Serves on the Assembly Aging, Children and Families, Cities, Governmental Operations, Housing, and Small Business Committees for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Joey Cohen-Saban
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the canceled Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot; lost to Novakhov by about 230 votes in 2024

summary.text: Joey Cohen-Saban is the Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Michael Novakhov in Assembly District 45, running again after losing to Novakhov by roughly 230 votes in 2024. He is a Brooklyn Democratic Party district leader and chief of staff to State Senator Sam Sutton.

background.text: A first-generation American who grew up in South Brooklyn and lives on the same block where he was raised.
Serves as a Brooklyn Democratic Party district leader and as chief of staff to State Senator Sam Sutton.
Says he led pro-Israel advocacy while a student at George Washington University.

priorities.text: Fighting antisemitism: "Antisemitic attacks in New York have surged to record levels. Joey Cohen-Saban will champion proactive legislation in Albany to protect all New Yorkers from rising antisemitism and hate crimes."

Education and yeshiva funding: will push to increase per-pupil funding, secure capital-improvement grants for aging school buildings, and ensure nonpublic schools including yeshivas get their fair share of state education dollars.
Neighborhood safety: supports strengthening ties between the community and local police precincts, more foot patrols, and community-policing initiatives.

Immigration and shelters: says migrant-shelter expansion has been handled irresponsibly and placed unfair burdens on residential neighborhoods, and that Albany should address current residents' housing, healthcare, and education needs before taking on new commitments.

positions.summary: Says he will be a strong, unwavering voice in Albany for the U.S.-Israel relationship and push back against efforts to undermine it.
positions.quote: The bond between the United States and Israel is a cornerstone of security and shared democratic values. Joey will be a strong, unwavering voice in Albany for the US-Israel relationship — pushing back against efforts to undermine this critical alliance.

positions.summary: Platform emphasizes securing state funding for yeshivas and other nonpublic schools alongside public schools.

sources.title: Assembly Bill A5214 - Not on our dollar!: Ending New York funding of Hamas violence act

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Novakhov's positions are drawn mainly from his campaign platform page and official bill sponsorships; neither candidate made a direct statement on federal immigration enforcement (ICE cooperation/deportations) specifically, so no position on that issue key is included for either, per the no-inference standard. Cohen-Saban's positions come from his campaign website; he has not held elected office, so he has no official voting or bill-sponsorship record.
